title: Local quasi-finiteness of scheme morphisms descends along fpqc coverings
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $\{u_i:T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering family [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. For every $i\in I$ let $f_i:X\times_T T_i\to T_i$ be the second projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. If every $f_i$ is locally quasi-finite in the scheme sense of [pqf-def-quasifinite], then $f$ is locally quasi-finite in the same sense, including local finite type. No quasi-compactness, separatedness or Noetherian hypothesis on $f$ is imposed; an fpqc family is not required to consist of quasi-compact morphisms.

source.place: Tag 02VI, lemma-descending-property-quasi-finite, locally quasi-finite assertion, descending direction.

proof.text: For each $i$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-locally-finite-type] to $f_i$, which is locally quasi-finite by hypothesis in the sense of [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Thus every $f_i$ is locally of finite type. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-locally-finite-type] to the given fpqc family and these second projections. It follows that $f$ is locally of finite type. This establishes the hypothesis needed for pointwise base-change reflection in step 3.

source.place: Tag 02VI (lemma-descending-property-quasi-finite), proof of the locally quasi-finite assertion.

proof.text: Write $a_i:X\times_TT_i\to X$ for the first projections. By [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change], applied to the given family along $f:X\to T$, the family $\{a_i\}$ is an fpqc covering of $X$. In particular it is jointly surjective by [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Given any $x\in X$, choose an affine neighbourhood $V$ of $x$; the finite affine opens in that definition have images covering $V$, so one contains a point $x_i$ with $a_i(x_i)=x$. This uses no surjectivity or quasi-compactness of any individual $u_i$.

source.place: Tag 022D (lemma-fpqc), part (3), and Tag 022B (definition-fpqc-covering); the covering-point choice implicit in Tag 02VI.

proof.text: Fix $x$ and its lift $x_i$ from step 2. Local quasi-finiteness of $f_i$ means that $f_i$ is quasi-finite at $x_i$ by [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Since $f$ is locally of finite type by step 1, [lem-sfb-scheme-quasifinite-at-base-change] applies to $f$, $u_i$, and $x_i$. Its reverse implication gives that $f$ is quasi-finite at $a_i(x_i)=x$. As $x$ was arbitrary, [pqf-def-quasifinite] gives local quasi-finiteness of $f$, with the same local finite-type requirement. If $X$ is empty there are no points to check, and this conclusion is the same universal statement.

The proof is exactly the Stacks proof of Tag 02VI (descent.tex line 6117). Step 1 shows f is locally of finite type, first for each f_i by lem-weil-pbc-lqf-locally-finite-type and then for f by lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-locally-finite-type (02KX); the objects and hypotheses of that lemma match the item exactly. Step 2 uses the 022D(3) leaf lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change with U=X and g=f, so the first projections a_i form an fpqc covering of X; joint surjectivity from def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering then lifts each point x to some x_i. Step 3 applies the reverse direction of lem-sfb-scheme-quasifinite-at-base-change (01TM(1); f locally of finite type by step 1, any base change; reviewed PASS by NV) at x_i, so f is quasi-finite at every x. The statement is unchanged and still unsplit in live and side-live. There are no new nodes, proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, and there is no cycle (210-node closure). The two declared tool_uses are generic scheme lemmas from sk-thm-p1 (01TD remark and 02KX) that no node of this unit states, and I accept them. Edge cases checked: empty X, empty cover, non-quasi-compact u_i, and an infinite disjoint union of points (locally quasi-finite but not quasi-finite). No fixes.
